target.name: Unspun
target.founder: Beth Esponnette, Walden Lam, Kevin Martin

methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $57M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 4 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Robotics & Manufacturing. Range: $1.1B - $2.0B.

data.narrative:
Unspun, a Series A robotics and manufacturing company founded by Beth Esponnette, Walden Lam, and Kevin Martin, has raised $57M to date. Valuation assessment draws on a comp universe of nine private robotics firms at Seed through Series B stages—including Bedrock Robotics, Dexterity, and Generalist AI—plus one public comparable.

Two valuation methods triangulate a defensible range. Stage-progression analysis applies a 2.0x multiplier to the $57M total raised as a proxy baseline, implying $114M. Peer-median analysis across four same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables yields a median valuation of $1.7B, with a range spanning $1.1B (Walden Robotics, Seed) to $2.0B (Generalist AI, Series B). The peer cohort reflects meaningful heterogeneity in stage and valuation, introducing material dispersion.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $97M (low) to $2.0B (high), with a median of $907M. The wide spread reflects genuine uncertainty around Unspun's competitive position within a heterogeneous peer set and the applicability of stage-progression heuristics to an early-stage robotics company. Key sensitivities include revenue trajectory, unit economics, and the strength of Unspun's technical differentiation relative to Bedrock and Dexterity peers. Further diligence on burn rate and path to Series B readiness would narrow this range materially.
